PullRequest.Title: Improve plugin marketplace browse output
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Formats `/plugin marketplace browse` results as structured Markdown at the command source, with a heading, code-styled plugin names, readable description separators, and escaped marketplace-provided text. Removes the generic text-list post-processor that is no longer needed.

This PR is stacked on #341787 and targets its `fix-copilot-plugin-commands` branch.

Fixes #339726

## Testing

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommand.test.ts --grep 'invokes plugin marketplace commands|defers to the runtime for unsupported and changed responses'` — 2 tests passed\n- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed\n- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotCustomizationCommandDisplay.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommand.test.ts` — passed\n\n## Manual test steps\n\n1. Open Chat and start a Copilot agent session.\n2. Run `/plugin marketplace browse awesome-copilot`.\n3. Verify the output has a `Plugins in awesome-copilot` heading.\n4. Verify each plugin is shown as a bullet with its name styled as inline code and its description separated by an em dash.\n5. Verify the output does not expose raw Markdown links or command links supplied by marketplace descriptions.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The callback implementation, serial command call path, and formatter guard are all directly traced. The exact RPC duration is environment-dependent, but the extra critical-path IPC and its uselessness for non-list commands are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: an SDK/subprocess `client.rpc.plugins.list()` IPC and its returned plugin inventory
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Adds one serialized inventory RPC for every `/plugin` command invocation, including browse, install, update, enable, disable, and error/usage responses where the inventory is never consumed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased command-result latency and unnecessary IPC/subprocess work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: `getOutput` formatted the already-returned plugin result synchronously and performed no additional inventory read.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The plugin branch now awaits `getInstalledPlugins()` before calling `formatCopilotPluginOutput`, even though that formatter immediately returns for every subcommand except empty/list/ls and for unsupported result shapes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 54 newly evaluates and awaits `getInstalledPlugins()` unconditionally in the `plugin` switch branch; the deleted implementation passed only `input` and `result` and had no boundary call.
Findings.Title: Gate the installed-plugin RPC to list output
Findings.Impact: Every plugin action now waits for a second SDK operation before its result is rendered. For example, marketplace browse completes its browse RPC and then serially performs an unrelated global plugin-list RPC; enable/disable already call `plugins.list()` in `findPlugin` and now call it again after mutation.
Findings.Evidence: `CopilotAgentSession` passes `options.getInstalledPlugins` into this handler, and that callback at `copilotAgent.ts:7217-7220` executes `client.rpc.plugins.list()`. The command path awaits `runtimeSlashCommand.getOutput` at `copilotAgentSession.ts:4764` before emitting output. `formatCopilotPluginOutput` checks the subcommand only after this await and returns undefined unless it is `''`, `list`, or `ls` (`copilotCustomizationCommandDisplay.ts:529-542`).
Findings.Recommendation: Check the normalized subcommand and supported plain-text list shape before invoking `getInstalledPlugins`; fetch the inventory only for `''`, `list`, or `ls` output that will actually be formatted.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The active-session before/after boundary count, serial awaits, editor retrigger path, and lack of coalescing are directly visible. Magnitude depends on SDK responsiveness and typing cadence, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: global and session SDK `plugins.list()` IPC calls and serialized plugin-inventory payloads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For an active session, each plugin argument completion request now performs two list RPCs instead of one; slash completions are requested while the user types, so cost grows with the number of keystrokes/retriggers and overlapping canceled requests are not coalesced.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased interactive completion latency, IPC traffic, and avoidable subprocess work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: When a live session existed, `_listInstalledPlugins` returned `session.listInstalledPlugins()`, issuing one session-scoped `plugins.list()` RPC per completion request. The global RPC was used only when no session existed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The method now awaits the global `client.rpc.plugins.list()` first and then, for a live session, awaits `session.listInstalledPlugins()` as a second sequential RPC before merging the inventories.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 4472 newly issues the global list before session lookup; the deleted branch returned the live session list immediately, so the active-session boundary count changes from one list RPC to two sequential list RPCs per request.
Findings.Title: Coalesce plugin inventory reads across completion requests
Findings.Impact: Typing plugin mutation arguments such as `/plugin update elastic...` repeatedly blocks suggestions on two serialized SDK calls. The editor keeps invoking agent-host completions throughout a slash-led token, and the completion provider ignores cancellation, so rapid typing can leave multiple doubled inventory requests in flight.
Findings.Evidence: The editor gate returns true for any input beginning with `/` (`chatInputCompletionUtils.ts:116-119`) and calls the agent host for each completion request (`agentHostInputCompletionsBase.ts:80-94`). The provider invokes `getInstalledPlugins` for plugin enable/disable/update/remove/uninstall prefixes (`copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts:166-186`), and its token is unused. `session.listInstalledPlugins()` is itself `this._wrapper.session.rpc.plugins.list()` (`copilotAgentSession.ts:1100-1102`). No inventory cache exists here, while the same provider explicitly uses a per-session promise/TTL cache for marketplace completions.
Findings.Recommendation: Coalesce a per-session inventory promise over the completion window (as the marketplace completion cache already does), invalidate it on plugin mutations/reload, and issue the global and session list calls in parallel when both snapshots are required.

Scenarios.Scenario: Execute a `/plugin` slash command, including marketplace browse and plugin mutations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command-specific SDK operation completes first; `CopilotAgentSession` then awaits the handler's `getOutput` before emitting any result. The diff places a global installed-plugin list RPC in that post-command stage, so it is on the result-rendering critical path even when formatting immediately rejects non-list subcommands.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one additional call per active-session `/plugin` invocation when the callback is present, independent of catalog size; enable/disable already perform a separate list during `findPlugin`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Output formatting consumed only the command result and made no post-command inventory RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs serially after the command-specific operation and must finish before output is emitted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform the requested install/update/enable/disable/reload or marketplace browse/list operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one command operation, with mutation commands also performing their existing list/reload sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same requested SDK operation ran before output formatting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the requested work and was already on the command critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of `/plugin` command invocations; marketplace browse formatting additionally scales linearly with returned plugins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one command the new inventory read is serialized after the requested operation. Separate command invocations follow normal session turn sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing is used for the new post-command inventory read. Marketplace browse data is consumed directly from its command result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: callback implementation, await placement, formatter guard, and output emission order are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC duration varies with runtime/subprocess load, but one extra critical-path RPC and its uselessness for non-list output are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager work: the inventory RPC is unconditional although only installed-plugin list formatting can consume it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request plugin enable/disable/update/remove/uninstall completions while typing in an active Copilot CLI chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench asks the agent host for completions throughout a slash-led token. The provider awaits installed plugins, then the newly added customization lookup, before returning suggestions. For a live session, installed plugins now require a global list RPC followed by the pre-existing session list RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request completion items from the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per editor completion retrigger while typing slash-command input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion bridge call occurred, but its active-session plugin inventory path performed one SDK list RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suggestions cannot render until the agent-host response returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly added call per matching plugin completion request in an active session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Skipped entirely when a live session existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before session lookup and before the existing session inventory call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per matching completion request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the sole inventory RPC for an active-session completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now runs after the new global list, making the two calls serial within each request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Settle customization discovery and initialize workspace `.mcp.json` discovery when cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold path can read one MCP definition file per effective workspace root and await initial customization scanning; initialized roots avoid repeat file reads, though each lookup still merges current snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The plugin branch returned before requesting session customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new `getSessionCustomizations` call must settle before plugin candidates return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of completion retriggers/keystrokes; inventory serialization also scales with installed plugin count, and cold customization discovery scales with workspace roots/customizations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The global and session list calls are serialized inside each request. The provider does not consume its cancellation token, so superseded typing requests can overlap; no shared limiter or promise coalesces inventory reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no installed-inventory cache. By contrast, marketplace completions in the same provider use a per-session promise/TTL cache. MCP root discovery caches initialized snapshots, so filesystem reads are cold-only unless watchers force refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: editor gating, provider branch, both SDK list implementations, serial awaits, and absent inventory coalescing are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Warm RPC latency and typing cadence vary; cold customization discovery prevalence is uncertain. The doubled active-session IPC count and per-request placement are not uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated boundary work: active-session inventory calls increase from one to two per completion request and are repeated across typing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover Copilot CLI-installed plugins at startup or after the CLI config changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The installed-plugin store reads/parses the CLI config, discovery resolves each effective plugin directory, and plugin contents are built before the aggregate discovery publishes. The diff records each plugin's enabled flag as an in-memory default during this existing scan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the Copilot CLI config file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read on cold discovery and one debounced read after relevant config watcher events; unchanged inventories are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same config read and parse occurred without retaining the `enabled` field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before initial Copilot CLI plugin discovery can publish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each distinct installed plugin URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve per deduplicated installed plugin from the cached config inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to validate each source before discovery publishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective number of distinct installed plugin cache paths after URI deduplication; disabled plugins determine the size of the added default-state map.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery resolves plugin directories sequentially as before; config watcher refreshes are debounced by 200 ms and unchanged inventories do not trigger a rebuild.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed installed inventory is cached until a changed config snapshot arrives. Added default enablement is in-memory observable state; enabled-by-default entries do not occupy the map, and uninstall through this discovery removes state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the existing filesystem boundaries and in-memory update behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users generally have modest plugin counts; external removal of disabled plugins can leave small in-memory default entries until process end, but no realistic unbounded or user-visible regression was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds bounded in-memory enablement bookkeeping to an already per-plugin filesystem scan and introduces no new expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Format marketplace browse results and installed-plugin lists as Markdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Marketplace browse escapes each returned name/description and joins lines after the browse result arrives. Installed-plugin list formatting scans runtime lines and the global inventory after the inventory callback completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Marketplace catalog entries and installed plugin entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Formatting is synchronous and linear for browse output. Installed-list matching can scan the inventory for each runtime line, but realistic plugin inventories are small and the dominant added boundary is accounted for in the command scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No formatting cache; each command formats its current result. This is appropriate for mutable command output.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the local formatting loops; no new external boundary exists in the formatter itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large marketplace catalogs increase escaping/allocation, but the deleted generic post-processor also parsed and escaped the same returned list, so a material allocation regression was not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: direct Markdown construction replaces equivalent generic processing without a proven asymptotic or material allocation increase.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and every diff hunk. Submitted two findings: unconditional post-command plugin inventory IPC, and doubled/uncoalesced inventory IPC on the per-keystroke active-session completion path. Checked command formatting, completion retriggers, SDK IPCs, cold/warm customization discovery, plugin config filesystem scans, observable enablement state, caching, and concurrency; no other high-confidence regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
